lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs shook off the opening-night sting and answered with purpose - and that matters in October, when tone can become habit. Easton Cowan's goal-and-assist night helped power a 2-1 win over the Islanders, the kind of brisk, youthful jolt this club has been begging for while Anthony Stolarz stood tall in net and turned aside nearly everything in sight. At 1-1-0, with 2 points and first place in the Atlantic Division, Toronto has put itself back on level ground after the 3-2 loss to Montreal, but nobody in this room should mistake a single sharp rebound for proof of arrival. The story right now is energy - some young juice, as the locals say, and a goalie who looked steady enough to calm a rattled building. Next up is Saturday against Ottawa, and the Leafs need to turn this into a runway, not a relay.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season didn't just end - it exposed a front office now forced into hard choices. Mark Shapiro backed Vladimir Guerrero Jr. after the star's own apology tour, a telling show of faith after a brutal year, and it matters because Toronto finished 79-83, fifth in the AL East, with no October to soften the blow. Guerrero is still the franchise's gravity well, but the club's own year-end message was plain: assess everything, fix the offense, and decide whether the current core is sturdy enough or merely familiar. The Blue Jays are heading into an offseason where patience, payroll and pride will all be tested at once. The next move is simple to name and hard to make - reshape the lineup without tearing up the roster.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Camp has a shape now, and it starts with a simple truth: Toronto's offense needs teeth. Kawhi Leonard's arrival is the league's biggest camp development, and the Raptors believe his pull-up shooting can drag their perimeter game out of the mud - a team that finished last season near the bottom from deep finally has a veteran who can bend a defense without begging for help. Scottie Barnes sounds eager to learn from a legend, and that matters; a young star's growth is often measured by the company he keeps. Toronto's next test comes Saturday against Miami in the first preseason tune-up, while the regular season opens Oct. 21 against Chicago. Watch Leonard's ramp-up, Barnes' fit, and whether Walter and Murray-Boyles keep turning heads.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders finally shook off the early wobble - and did it with some bite. Marcus Mariota steered a 33-31 upset of the Seahawks, the kind of win that can steady a locker room and quiet a sour start. Washington sits 1-2, third in the NFC East, one game back, and that's not pretty - but it's alive. Jayden Daniels' elbow remains the headline; he returned to limited practice Wednesday, yet his status for London is still uncertain. For now, the Commanders are leaning on toughness and improvisation, the old NFL currencies. Mariota earned the day. Next comes the Colts on Sunday in London - and Daniels' availability may decide whether this first spark becomes a real run.

article.title: Maple Leafs Beat Islanders Behind Stolarz
paragraphs: Anthony Stolarz stopped 26 shots and the Maple Leafs beat the Islanders 2-1 on Wednesday night, with Easton Cowan scoring once and adding an assist and Colton Sissons also finding the net. Toronto is back at it Saturday against the Senators, while the Blue Jays are in offseason mode after a year with few firm plans and the Raptors keep building toward their Oct. 21 regular-season opener against the Bulls.

For Washington, Jayden Daniels returned to practice in limited fashion, but his status for Sunday's game against the Colts in London remains uncertain. The Commanders are 1-2, and the next checkpoint is their 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff on NFL Network.
